checked.found: April 30, 1789, oath on the second-floor balcony of Federal Hall, New York (NPS)
March 4, 1797, Congress Hall, Philadelphia; Washington retired after two terms
March 4, 1801, first inauguration held in Washington, D.C.; 1800 election decided by the House on the 36th ballot
March 4, 1809; Wikipedia and the White House Historical Association say his outfit was American-made wool. 'Principal author of the Constitution' is standard.
March 4, 1817; House/Senate dispute over seating (senators' armchairs) pushed the ceremony outdoors, first outdoor oath
Elected by the House on Feb 9, 1825 after no candidate won an electoral majority; inaugurated March 4, 1825
1829; crowds at the White House reception broke china and furniture (White House Historical Association)
March 4, 1841; longest inaugural address (about 8,445 words, 1h45m), cold wet day; died April 4, 1841 (cause disputed, 'illness' is safe)
March 4, 1845; first dark horse nominee of a major party; rain; first inauguration reported by telegraph (Wikipedia)
March 4, 1861; soldiers and sharpshooters guarded the route; address appealed to the seceded states
March 4, 1869; Andrew Johnson skipped the ceremony
March 4, 1885; first Democrat elected since before the Civil War (24 years); bachelor; married in the White House in 1886, the only president to do so
March 4, 1897; Wikipedia and the Senate list it as the first inauguration recorded on film
September 14, 1901, Ansley Wilcox house, Buffalo; age 42, youngest person sworn in as president
March 4, 1909; blizzard moved the oath into the Senate chamber; sources agree Taft was the heaviest president (peak ~320-340+ lb)

Inauguration was March 4, 1913. The Woman Suffrage Procession was on March 3, the day before, and drew the crowds away from Wilson's arrival. The description places the march at the inauguration itself.
checked.suggestion: A former Princeton professor and governor became the first Democratic president in sixteen years, a day after a huge suffrage march overshadowed his arrival.

checked.found: March 4, 1921; Ohio History Connection: first president to give an amplified inaugural address via a public address system; 'return to normalcy' campaign line
March 4, 1929; engineer and wartime relief administrator; optimistic address; crash seven months later
March 4, 1933; 'the only thing we have to fear is fear itself'; unemployment over 25%
April 12, 1945, about two hours after learning of Roosevelt's death; formerly a Missouri senator, then vice president
January 20, 1953; opened with a prayer he composed himself; first Republican president in 20 years
January 20, 1961; youngest elected president (43); bitterly cold and clear day after snow
November 22, 1963, Air Force One at Love Field, Jacqueline Kennedy at his side
January 20, 1969; lost the 1960 election to Kennedy; address centred on Vietnam. The 1960 margin and the domestic division were not in the results but are well known.
January 20, 1977; walked the mile and a half from the Capitol to the White House; peanut farming ties
January 20, 1981; oldest person to take office until 2017 (69y 349d); hostages in Iran freed that day
January 20, 1989; 'kinder, gentler' theme; Reagan's vice president; Director of Central Intelligence 1976-77
January 20, 1993; Maya Angelou read 'On the Pulse of Morning'; first baby boomer president, aged 46
January 20, 2001; Bush v. Gore halted the Florida recount; son of the 41st president
